description: Qantas Points and Status Credits for flights marketed by Qantas (QF), from Qantas's earning tables: a fixed amount per flight by route table (or distance band) and earn category (cat; get_fare_classes for QF shows which booking classes fall in each category), plus the Status Bonus (points only) and the Minimum Points Guarantee. Give segs: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them), the ISO country codes of its two airports, and from/to IATA airport codes: Qantas picks its route tables (Sydney to London, Perth to Singapore, Sydney to Dallas and so on) from the airports, so without from/to a flight such as Australia to Europe falls back to the distance band. For the USA and Canada, which Qantas splits into East and West Coast tables without listing cities, set table on that flight (for example EWC or EEC); table BND forces the distance band. Takes no price. Uses cwsi.net's calculator and the airline's published rules. Unofficial.

cat.description: Earn category. DE = Discount Economy (E N O Q; dom. E G L M N O Q S V); EC = Economy (G K L M S V); FE = Flexible Economy (B H Y; dom. B H K Y); DPE = Discount Premium Economy (T; dom. T); PE = Premium Economy (R; dom. R); FPE = Flexible Premium Economy (W; dom. W); DB = Discount Business (I); BU = Business (D; dom. D I); FB = Flexible Business (C J; dom. C J); FI = First (A F). The fare type on your ticket. Under each: the international booking classes, then the classes on flights within Australia (dom.). On domestic flights there is no Discount Business; class I is Business.

creditClass.description: The booking class letter on the ticket, for creditTo (required with creditTo). Ignored without creditTo.

creditFlights.description: The flights for creditTo: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them) and optionally from/to airport codes. Defaults to segs when they carry miles.

from.description: The departure airport's code; labels the breakdown.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

to.description: The arrival airport's code; labels the breakdown.

creditStatus.description: Your status in the creditTo program, by its name as listed under creditTo. Defaults to the base level. Ignored without creditTo.

creditTo.description: Credit the flights to a partner program instead of Qantas's own: american = American AAdvantage (creditStatus one of: AAdvantage member, AAdvantage Gold, AAdvantage Platinum, AAdvantage Platinum Pro, AAdvantage Executive Platinum); alaska = Atmos Rewards (creditStatus one of: Atmos Rewards member, Atmos Silver, Atmos Gold, Atmos Platinum, Atmos Titanium); flying-blue = Flying Blue (creditStatus one of: Explorer, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Ultimate); ba-club = British Airways Club (creditStatus one of: Blue, Bronze, Silver, Gold). Earns by each flight's distance and the booking class at the program's published partner rates; leave creditTo out for the airline's own program. Give the booking class letter as creditClass. The flights are segs (their miles), or creditFlights.

sc.description: Status Credits you have so far (optional). Used only for the progress toward the next tier.

segs.description: The flights, one way and in order, one entry per flight (1 to 8): fromCountry and toCountry, the ISO 3166 two-letter country codes of its two airports; miles, its great-circle distance in miles (1 to 12,500); optional table, the key of a route table for that flight (ENZ, EAS, EHI, EIN, EJB, ESC, EDF, EWC, EEC, WSE, WNE, WDX, WEU, WJB, NDF, NSC, NEC, DEC, DWC, CWC, XEU, UAS, THK, BND); optional from and to, the IATA codes of its two airports, which label the breakdown and pick the route tables named by airport.

from.description: The departure airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

fromCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the departure airport, e.g. DE.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

table.description: The route table for this flight, when the airports alone do not settle it (Qantas: the East or West Coast USA/Canada tables). ENZ = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and New Zealand or Papua New Guinea; EAS = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and Northeast Asia or Southeast Asia; EHI = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and Hawaii; EIN = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and Delhi or Bengaluru; EJB = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and Johannesburg; ESC = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and Santiago; EDF = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and Dallas; EWC = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and West Coast USA/Canada or Dubai; EEC = Between Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne or Sydney and East Coast USA/Canada or Europe; WSE = Between Darwin or Perth and Southeast Asia; WNE = Between Darwin or Perth and Northeast Asia; WDX = Between Darwin or Perth and Dubai; WEU = Between Darwin or Perth and Europe; WJB = Between Darwin or Perth and Johannesburg; NDF = Between New Zealand and Dallas; NSC = Between New Zealand and Santiago; NEC = Between New Zealand and East Coast USA/Canada; DEC = Between Dallas and East Coast USA/Canada; DWC = Between Dallas and West Coast USA/Canada; CWC = Between East Coast USA/Canada and West Coast USA/Canada; XEU = Between Dubai and Europe, Northern Africa or Southeast Asia; UAS = Between Europe and Northeast Asia or Southeast Asia; THK = Between Tel Aviv and Hong Kong; BND = Distance band (no route table)

to.description: The arrival airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

toCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the arrival airport, e.g. DE.

status.description: Your Qantas Frequent Flyer tier. BR = Bronze; SV = Silver (+50% points); GD = Gold (+75% points); PL = Platinum (+100% points); P1 = Platinum One (+100% points). The Status Bonus adds Qantas Points, never Status Credits.

trip.description: Trip. ow = One way; rt = Round trip. Round trip counts the same flights back the other way.
